summary: Summation No. 35, the final issue of the series, covers August 1948 (statistics mostly for June-July) and carries a Review of the Third Occupation Year (1 September 1947 - 31 August 1948). Politically the month is dominated by the Ashida cabinet's cabinet order and planned revision of the National Public Service Law following MacArthur's July letter, labor unrest on the railways, argument over dissolving the Diet and a proposed centrist league, the Illegal Transactions Investigation Committee hearings (Nishio acquitted, Nakasone sentenced), the Fukui-Ishikawa earthquake damage to textile mills, and MacArthur's address at the inauguration of the Republic of Korea. Economic parts cover SCAP's removal of export controls (15-18 August), a sterling-area trade plan, price stabilization, hoarded goods, the Reconstruction Finance Bank, holding-company dissolution and reparations shipments. Long statistical sections give production of coal, metals, chemicals, textiles, power, communications, labor, trade, prices, finance, science, patents, health and education, useful for quantifying recovery. The appendix surveys the third Occupation year.
highlights: MacArthur addressed the 15 August inauguration of the Republic of Korea in Seoul, calling Korea's division an artificial barrier to be torn down.
July cabinet order denied government employees strikes and collective bargaining; Cabinet interpretation 11 August; Shikoku absenteeism cancelled 118 trains on 16 August.
Former deputy prime minister Nishio acquitted 27 August; Nakasone sentenced to four years 31 August in the Army Uniform Case.
SCAP authorized elimination of major Japanese Government controls on export trade, 15-18 August, letting foreign buyers deal directly with sellers.
Holding Company Liquidation Commission issued its first final reorganization order 22 August (Japan Soda Company split into six companies).
Fukui-Ishikawa earthquake damaged 686 of 1,774 textile mills; Reconstruction Finance Bank supplied about 1.1 billion yen for repair.
Japanese B encephalitis hit about 4,100 people with 219 deaths by 28 August; equine encephalomyelitis killed 522 horses.
Review of third Occupation year: industrial production index rose from 43.1 to 59.9; Japan's cumulative trade deficit reached about 822.8 million dollars.

sections.title: Front matter
sections.summary: Archive cover, notice that this is the final issue of the Summation, title page, table of contents and list of charts and tables (108 numbered charts).

sections.title: Part I: General
sections.summary: Short digest of the month in four sections: SCAP organization, political, economic and social activities.

sections.title: Section 1. Organization Under SCAP
sections.summary: One sentence: no change in the non-military organization of GHQ SCAP in August.

sections.title: Section 2. Political Activities
sections.summary: Digest of MacArthur at Seoul, constitutional revision, Public Service Law debate, Diet dissolution, centrist realignment, court decisions, dissolved ultranationalist groups, public safety figures and war crimes trials.

sections.title: Section 3. Economic Activities
sections.summary: Digest of agriculture, mining, industrial output, rail unrest, power, communications, labor, trade controls lifted 15 August, food rations, finance, property control, antitrust and science items.

sections.title: Section 4. Social Activities
sections.summary: Digest of encephalitis epidemics, public assistance increases, repatriation of 44,400, Board of Education Law, university reorganization, religion and press items.

sections.title: Part II: Political
sections.summary: Government and politics, public safety, legal affairs and war crimes.

sections.title: Section 1. Government and Politics
sections.summary: MacArthur and Ashida messages, constitutional revision study, Public Service Law cabinet order, dissolution disputes, party maneuvers, local elections, corruption hearings, purge cases and economic policy statements.

sections.title: Supreme Commander's Statement to Republic of Korea
sections.summary: Text of MacArthur's 15 August Seoul address to President Rhee: friendship since 1882, the artificial division of Korea, and defense of liberty.

sections.title: Prime Minister's Message on Anniversary of Defeat
sections.summary: Ashida's 15 August message: improving living conditions, falling inflation, and a call for a middle path and peace-loving reconstruction.

sections.title: Constitutional Revision Proposals
sections.summary: Diet leaders agree 20 August on a joint committee to study revision; six topics listed, including the Emperor's ceremonial role and Diet conflicts.

sections.title: Political Developments: National Public Service Law Discussion
sections.summary: Text of the cabinet order banning strikes and collective bargaining, labor and Communist reaction, Cabinet interpretation of 11 August, social democratic seven-point plan and cabinet disagreements.

sections.title: Problem of Diet Dissolution
sections.summary: Government parties split on dissolving the Diet; Ashida wants delay to end of year, Katayama and left-wing Social Democrats want a November election.

sections.title: Prime Minister's Address to Foreign Correspondents
sections.summary: Ashida's 27 August speech on food, clothing, slowing inflation, labor, political stability and middle-of-the-road policy.

sections.title: Political Parties
sections.summary: Debate over a Middle Course Political League, Democratic, Social Democratic, People's Cooperative and Democratic Liberal positions, and minor parties including the Communists.

sections.title: Local Government
sections.summary: Recall of a Saitama village mayor upheld on a tied recount; independent elected governor in an August prefectural election.

sections.title: Illegal Transactions Investigations
sections.summary: Nishio acquitted, Nakasone Army Uniform Case sentences, Kano case, Area Disposal and coal-mine bribery hearings, new charges against Miki and Kitamura.

sections.title: The Purge
sections.summary: Ultranationalist groups dissolved in August; 377,788 screened and 201,333 purged by month end; indictments for purge violations.

sections.title: Economic Plans and Policies
sections.summary: Government pledge to the ESB ten-point policy, financial reorganization plan, wage dispute over the National Personnel Authority, payroll cuts, party anti-inflation and reconstruction programs.

sections.title: Section 2. Public Safety
sections.summary: Hoarded goods (5.95 million yen recovered in July), black-market and bribery cases, June crime and arrest statistics, police actions, prison population, fires, and transfer of offshore policing to Maritime Safety Board.

sections.title: Section 3. Legal Affairs and War Crimes
sections.summary: Supreme Court caseload, judicial conferences, domestic relations court, atrocity investigation table, 70 suspects apprehended, 713 tried to date; seven trials in the period, two death sentences; IMTFE in recess.

sections.title: Part III: Business
sections.summary: Fourteen economic sections with extensive production, trade, price, finance and science statistics.

sections.title: Section 1. Agriculture and Fisheries
sections.summary: Agricultural cooperative program and cabinet orders, Kanto Plain soil survey, mulberry and illegal tobacco growing, livestock, June marine catch fall to 150,018 tons, tuna export rejections, petroleum allocations and whaling.

sections.title: Agricultural cooperatives and administration
sections.summary: Dissolution of agricultural associations, posters, and three August cabinet orders on property transfers to cooperatives.

sections.title: Fisheries
sections.summary: Smaller sardine and mackerel catches, spoilage from lack of ice, a new purse seiner, August fuel allocations and 2,210 tons of whale products.

sections.title: Section 2. Forestry and Mining
sections.summary: Forestry charts, August coal output 3,542,000 tons (down about 300,000), deliveries and stockpiles, lignite, crude oil strike effects and drilling, and June mineral output with mercury up.

sections.title: Coal, oil and mining industry
sections.summary: Coal production by district, deliveries 2,669,000 tons in July, stockpiles, lignite, crude oil and mine production.

sections.title: Section 3. Industrial Raw Materials
sections.summary: July coke 264,112 tons; pig iron and rolled steel at postwar peaks; light metals, copper, zinc, petroleum refining, cement down 12 percent, chemicals, salt and pulp and paper figures.

sections.title: Coke and metal industries
sections.summary: Coke production, deliveries and stocks; iron, steel, aluminum, copper, zinc, tin and ferroalloys; petroleum products.

sections.title: Cement, chemicals, salt, pulp and paper
sections.summary: Cement output down for coal and transport shortages; 21 of 28 chemicals up; caustic soda postwar peak; salt output up 50.6 percent; paper postwar peak.

sections.title: Section 4. Machinery, Equipment and Construction
sections.summary: Machine tools, small tools, bearings, industrial and textile machinery, rolling stock and railway cars, electrical and communications equipment, truck output 1,388, coal miners' housing and building permits.

sections.title: Section 5. Manufactured Goods
sections.summary: June food processing, brewing, cigarettes up 12.3 percent, glass, ceramics, rubber, leather, handicrafts, business machines, musical instruments, watches, sewing machines, cosmetics, plus ship completions and the Soviet tug contract.

sections.title: Section 6. Textile Industries
sections.summary: Fukui-Ishikawa earthquake damage to mills, raw cotton imports, cotton, raw silk at postwar peak of 11,521 bales, rayon, wool, bast fibers, knit goods and dyeing, with stock and machinery tables.

sections.title: Earthquake damage
sections.summary: Survey recommends 1.514 billion yen for repairs; 686 of 1,774 mills damaged; Reconstruction Finance Bank to lend 1.12 billion yen.

sections.title: Cotton
sections.summary: Imports rose to 43.9 million pounds in July; spinners' supplies, yarn and fabric production and machinery.

sections.title: Silk
sections.summary: Raw silk production and stocks, testing, reeling mills, cocoon supplies, spun silk yarn and silk fabrics.

sections.title: Artificial fibers and wool
sections.summary: Rayon pulp imports, caustic soda bottleneck, rayon yarn and fabric; raw wool imports from Australia and South America.

sections.title: Hard and bast fibers, spun and reprocessed materials, knit goods, sundries, dyeing
sections.summary: Rope and cordage, jute and flax, thrown-spun and reprocessed yarns, knit goods, fish nets and fabrics processed.

sections.title: Section 7. Transportation and Public Utilities
sections.summary: Railway unrest in Shikoku, 519.9 million passengers, coal consumption, directive to Japan to assume port operations, coastwise shipping, July electric power 2.94 billion kWh and gas industry figures.

sections.title: Railways and water transportation
sections.summary: Communist-led absenteeism on Shikoku, 956 discharged; 17 August directive on port and terminal operations; coastal and foreign cargo.

sections.title: Electric power and gas
sections.summary: Generation, consumption, coal allocations, plant construction and public gas production and distribution.

sections.title: Section 8. Communications
sections.summary: 1,386,084 telephones after Telephone Bond Law, radio frequency changes, 6,858,814 licensed radio listeners, postal volume drop after the 11 July rate rise, postal insurance and personnel.

sections.title: Section 9. Labor
sections.summary: Labor rally against the Ashida cabinet, union statistics, Hokkaido and Imperial Oil disputes, labor schools, wage increases for Occupation workers, labor standards inspections, women and minors.

sections.title: Labor relations and disputes
sections.summary: Hokkaido railway walkout, coal wage agreement, electric power dispute, Imperial Oil mediation, Toho studio eviction.

sections.title: Employment and unemployment
sections.summary: Employment Security Advisory Committee, coal mine employment recheck, vocational training and unemployment insurance.

sections.title: Section 10. Imports and Exports
sections.summary: Export controls eliminated, sterling-area trade plan for 242 million dollars, 10 million dollars of cotton contracts, Siam talks, June trade by country and commodity, first-half deficit of 271 million dollars.

sections.title: Section 11. Price and Distribution
sections.summary: Record summer vegetable harvest, fish and sugar distribution, three more price stabilization groups, textile prices up about 90 percent, consumer price index 342.9, incentive goods and surplus Army cigarettes; economic enforcement text continues on page 111.

sections.title: Section 12. Finance
sections.summary: Economic Investigation Board created 1 August; notes in circulation 264 billion yen; Reconstruction Finance Bank plan; securities sales, closing of 18 control associations, tax revenue, first prison terms for tax evasion, national debt.

sections.title: Section 13. Property Control and Reparations
sections.summary: Looted property status, Attorney-General to liquidate dissolved organizations, custody accounts, restricted company expenditures, holding company orders, Fair Trade Commission filings and machine tool shipments to claimants.

sections.title: Section 14. Science and Technology
sections.summary: New Industrial Technique Management Council, research funds, travel of Japanese physicists to Princeton, standards, FEC access to Japanese processes, patent statistics, and a long background survey of Japan's climate.

sections.title: Patents and standards
sections.summary: Forty Japanese Standards issued in July, FEC technical access order of 6 August, patent and utility-model statistics and prospective inventions.

sections.title: Climate of Japan
sections.summary: Storm tracks, typhoons, vegetation zones, rice and crop limits, frost, precipitation, ocean currents, temperature and hail.

sections.title: Part IV: Social
sections.summary: Public health and welfare; education, religion, cultural resources and media.

sections.title: Section 1. Public Health and Welfare
sections.summary: Japanese B encephalitis and equine epidemics, training courses, model health centers, medical supplies, narcotics, public assistance and Fukui earthquake aid, social security, vital statistics, population density and repatriation of 44,625.

sections.title: Medical administration and supply
sections.summary: Veterinary and inspection data, nursing courses, production of penicillin, DDT, X-ray equipment and distribution of supplies.

sections.title: Narcotics, public assistance and social security
sections.summary: Handler registrations, welfare payments, new allowance rates, LARA shipments, 40 percent medical fee increase and insurance statistics.

sections.title: Vital statistics, population and repatriation
sections.summary: June birth rate lowest since 1929; population 80,170,815; census density maps; 6,024,896 repatriated by 2 September.

sections.title: Section 2. Education, Religion, Cultural Resources and Media of Expression
sections.summary: Teachers' union cabinet ordinance, Board of Education Law and October elections, curriculum recommendations, university reorganization, textbooks, religion, press comment, Asahi Saitama case, radio, films and SCAP libraries.

sections.title: Education
sections.summary: Redefined relations with the teachers' union, Board of Education Law, 219 university applications, textbooks and libraries.

sections.title: Religion, cultural resources and media of expression
sections.summary: Buddhist reform, Christian missions, press and radio themes, motion pictures and two new SCAP libraries.

sections.title: Appendix: Review of the Third Occupation Year (1 September 1947 - 31 August 1948)
sections.summary: Year-end review covering SCAP organization, economic recovery, living conditions and progress of democratization.

sections.title: Section 1. Organization Under SCAP
sections.summary: Restitution Advisory Committee established 13 April; no other organizational change during the year; chart of GHQ organization follows.

sections.title: Section 2. Economic Recovery
sections.summary: Coal and power, industrial production index 43.1 to 59.9, textiles, trade and sterling arrangements, transport, communications, finance, property control and reparations over the year.

sections.title: Section 3. Living Conditions
sections.summary: Nutrition, ration distribution, housing and rents, textile distribution, wage and price inflation, disaster relief, disease campaigns, health and child welfare laws; welfare and repatriation continue to page 165.

sections.title: Section 4. Progress of Democratization
sections.summary: Diet sessions and reforms, police and civil service laws, Tribunal and war crimes totals, agrarian reform, antitrust, labor, education, religion, media and science.
